NaturalProductMech

3136 natural product structures, one record per Standard InChIKey, harmonized from 10 adopted sources.

Search

A producer is not an occurrence. This corpus keeps the two apart because most sources do not. 3441 producer claims say a taxon makes the compound, and only 840 of those rest on evidence that addressed the organism. 2351 records carry a cited occurrence, which says only that someone found the compound there. Nothing promotes one to the other.

Chemical structure map

This view places 3136 records using chemical structure only: chiral Morgan count fingerprints and Tanimoto distance, projected to two dimensions with UMAP. Labels, filing pathways, producers, and curation fields can color or filter the view, but they do not affect position.

Read local neighborhoods, not the axes or global spacing. UMAP preserves nearby structure better than map-wide distance. Current full-corpus trustworthiness@10 is 0.975 and 2D neighbor overlap@10 is 0.535. Multi-fragment structures are retained exactly as their records define them and are visibly marked.

Corpus map

3114 compounds projected from their record text into two dimensions (PACMAP over BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5).

Proximity means described similarly: same pathway, family, activity, producing organism, where it was found. Not structurally similar.

Pathways separate without the projection being told them: 84% of a compound's ten nearest neighbours share its filing pathway, against a 20% baseline. Measured on this corpus, not inherited. That is a property of the map you are looking at — the underlying embedding scores 83%, and PaCMAP tightens neighbourhoods by construction.

Proximity means described similarly — same pathway, family, activity and producer — not structurally similar. These are text embeddings of what the corpus says about a compound; SMILES and InChI are deliberately excluded, because a sentence model reads them as noise. A chemical-similarity map is a different artifact.
